purpose: Test whether preparation, blinding, lineage, measurement-repeat, and integrity gates can be executed without changing the RC26 80-percent negative-alarm and 90-percent positive-evidence thresholds. Three batches are not an efficacy test.

claimBoundary.pilotClaim: The dry run can establish only that the ledger and adjudication workflow detect designed violations. A later three-batch physical pilot can estimate operational variance and cost but cannot qualify intervention efficacy.
claimBoundary.independentUnit: One independently weighed and mixed preparation session is one batch-level experimental unit. Its specimens, aliquots, scans, and analysis views are nested observations.
claimBoundary.lotScope: The three pilot batches reuse source lots and therefore target preparation repeatability conditional on those lots. They cannot support unconditional material-lot or institution transport.
claimBoundary.dictionaryScope: Complete-dictionary and omitted-Bi2O3 analyses are two blinded views of the same raw acquisition, never two physical specimens or two independent outcomes.
claimBoundary.confirmatoryBoundary: The fifteen-batch RC26 certificate remains separate. Pilot outcomes may change operations or terminate the program, but may not tune the sealed 0.80 and 0.90 thresholds. Any substantive intervention change requires a new confirmatory protocol before additional outcomes.

materialSystem.name: D1-D2 anchored barite-bismite-graphite mixture

components.role: bismite phase, high-absorption contrast, and sealed omitted-phase positive

particleArms.mixed-coarse: Thirty percent of graphite mass is retained above 90 micrometres and seventy percent passes 90 micrometres, matching the published D2 encoding.

materialSystem.selectionReason: Preselecting graphite size before mixing changes the intended particle-orientation handle without mechanically treating the complete mixture. This reduces, but does not eliminate, chemical and contamination confounding relative to whole-mixture milling.
materialSystem.notQualifiedBeyond: This composition does not represent other phase chemistries, amorphous components, nanoparticles, reactive mixtures, or unknown phases with weak or overlapping reflections.

primaryContrast.negativeEndpoint: One minus the complete-dictionary alarm under intervention divided by the baseline alarm; success threshold remains at least 0.80.
primaryContrast.positiveEndpoint: Omitted-Bi2O3 candidate evidence under intervention divided by baseline candidate evidence; success threshold remains at least 0.90.
primaryContrast.conservativeNearThresholdRule: A batch can pass only when the lower uncertainty bound clears the threshold. An interval crossing a threshold is unresolved and counts as non-success in confirmation.

diagnosticContrasts: fine|stationary-flat-plate versus mixed-coarse|stationary-flat-plate isolates the graphite-size branch conditional on flat-plate loading.
mixed-coarse|rotating-capillary versus mixed-coarse|stationary-flat-plate isolates the geometry branch conditional on mixed-coarse graphite.
The size-by-geometry interaction tests whether the combined intervention can be decomposed; no component receives an efficacy claim in the pilot.
physicalDesign.scheduleBoundary: The schedule is sealed for workflow testing, not claimed to be a fully balanced design. Technical repeat 2 follows repeat 1 within each randomized aliquot block so short-term repeatability is estimable without being counted as a new batch.

oneToMany: One source-lot tuple can feed multiple preparation batches.
One batch contains one fine and one mixed-coarse specimen.
One specimen is divided into stationary-flat-plate and rotating-capillary aliquots.
One aliquot has two technical acquisitions.
One raw acquisition receives a complete and an omitted-Bi2O3 analysis view.
forbiddenIndependenceClaims: specimensPerBatch, aliquotsPerBatch, acquisitions, and analyses cannot replace batch n
a renamed or copied aliquot, acquisition, or raw hash is not a new unit
common source lots cannot support unconditional across-lot transport
analysis-view disagreement cannot be repaired by rerunning the same raw file until it passes

blindingAndEmbargo.manufacturing: Preparation personnel know particle-size arms because they must construct them.
blindingAndEmbargo.acquisition: Instrument operators receive opaque aliquot codes and a sequence, not particle or dictionary labels.
blindingAndEmbargo.analysis: Analysts receive opaque acquisition codes and one of two sealed dictionary bundles. The omitted-phase identity is held by an adjudicator until all analysis outputs are hash-bound.
blindingAndEmbargo.dryRun: Committed fixtures use synthetic hashes and contain no physical measurements. Their demonstration codes must never be reused for a physical run.
blindingAndEmbargo.physicalOutcomeEmbargo: No endpoint estimate, pass flag, or integrity result may enter a dry-run ledger. In a physical pilot, outcome fields remain sealed until every expected raw hash and analysis output is present.

measurementAndIntegrity.gravimetry: Record masses and calibrated-balance identity for every component; absolute deviation of any nominal phase fraction above one percentage point fails composition integrity.
measurementAndIntegrity.particleSize: Record sieve identifiers, sieve-integrity check, retained and passing masses, and microscopy or an independently calibrated particle-size measurement on reserved material.
measurementAndIntegrity.diffraction: Preserve raw frames or the earliest instrument output, acquisition geometry, wavelength, detector configuration, sample spinning, exposure history, instrument-resolution reference, and every later transformation.
measurementAndIntegrity.transmission: Measure or estimate absorption in the exact acquisition geometry; XRF cannot provide carbon closure and is not the sole composition truth.
measurementAndIntegrity.phaseIntegrity: Compare reserved input materials and prepared specimens using full-profile XRPD plus Raman or another orthogonal phase-sensitive method. Contamination, a new peak, polymorph change, or unexplained broadening quarantines the batch.
measurementAndIntegrity.technicalRepeats: Use two acquisitions per aliquot to estimate acquisition repeatability and threshold uncertainty. Average or model them within batch; never count them as independent batches.

safetyAndAuthority.executionGate: The repository does not authorize laboratory work. Physical execution requires local EHS approval, current supplier SDS review, trained powder handling, registered and interlocked X-ray equipment, and an equipment-specific operating procedure.
safetyAndAuthority.powderControl: Use micrometre-scale materials, closed transfer or local exhaust, minimum feasible mass, suitable eye and skin protection, and institutional respiratory-protection decisions. Do not use nanopowders or openly aerosolize, brush, blow, or dry-mill graphite.
safetyAndAuthority.radiation: Never bypass diffractometer shielding or interlocks. Record tube, shutter, exposure, and instrument-registration information required by the jurisdiction.
safetyAndAuthority.waste: Segregate powder and contaminated consumables according to supplier SDS and local chemical-waste rules; do not release bismuth-containing powder to the environment.
safetyAndAuthority.stop: Stop on dust escape, damaged capillary, interlock or ventilation failure, unidentified contamination, unexpected heat or reaction, broken blinding, or a mismatch between physical labels and committed hashes.

readinessGates.pass: Local EHS and radiation officers approve the exact materials, scale, enclosure, instrument, and waste route.
The valid dry-run ledger passes and every adversarial fixture is rejected for its intended reason.
An independent dry run demonstrates offline arm-map custody, pre-outcome commitments, and one-time unblinding.
Instrument-resolution, geometry, transmission, exposure, raw-data export, and Raman or orthogonal integrity procedures are fixed.
Supplier lots, purity certificates, sieve fractions, balance calibration, and reserved reference materials are available.
